notes:
- Digital signatures, with no third-party signing service. Tumbler creates
  your signing identity on your own machine and keeps the private key in your
  system keychain, then adds a real ISO-standard signature that Adobe Acrobat
  and other readers can verify. File ▸ Digitally Sign & Save…
- Signatures can include a trusted timestamp from a free public service, so
  the signing time is independently verifiable. It falls back to your
  computer clock if you are offline. Turn it off in Settings if you prefer.
- Click the status-bar shield to verify a signed document: it confirms the
  document is unchanged, shows the signer, and lets you trust that signer so
  future documents from them show as trusted.
- Optional trust directory on getflanders.com: publish your signing
  certificate so people you send documents to can confirm it belongs to your
  email address. Only your public certificate is shared, never your key.
